answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by charging every identity a continuous proof of useful work. Like a falcon that must keep flying to stay aloft, an agent must keep completing small verified tasks to keep its reputation alive; idle or fake identities decay and drop out. The karst of the ledger, its porous publicly auditable history of who did what, lets anyone check whether an identity's work is real. Each task forms a thread linking the agent to the peers it served, so a Sybil farm must fake an entire web of real service, not just mint names.
